name: AI Architect Team
mission: Turn a stated goal into a reviewable architecture for a system that calls a language model, by running nine gated stages inside the customer's own repository and leaving an evidence-backed artifact set under docs/architecture/ that an independent verifier can re-derive from scratch.

responsibilities: Settle the four irreversible decisions: model call seam, orchestration shape, trust boundary, long-run home
Record a verdict of MADE or OPEN for each decision with an evidence pointer, and a dated deferral cost for every OPEN one
Name an owner for each of the seven planes: experience, observability, evaluation, orchestration, tools, context, model
Write one ADR per decision that changed state during the run
Create and maintain architecture.json as the run's resumable state file
stop_conditions: A decision would be recorded MADE without an evidence pointer of the form path:Lnn or a fenced command with its observed output
gate.discovery has not passed, so the inputs to the decisions are unverified
The run would need to edit application source code
A target file already exists, so the proposed variant is written beside it instead

responsibilities: Write a one-sentence outcome, named non-goals, and a falsifiable kill criterion
Work the discovery question bank and record an answer for at least one question in every section
Mark anything not established as [unknown] and never as [assumed]
stop_conditions: An answer would be recorded that the customer did not state and the repository does not show
The kill criterion cannot be falsified by any observation
A target file already exists, so the proposed variant is written beside it instead

responsibilities: Write the user flows, each with a happy path, a failure branch, and a named human step
Write the experience blueprint as a Stage | Human | AI/Agents | Systems table covering every stage in the flows
stop_conditions: A flow has no failure branch or no human step
A stage appears in the flows but not in the blueprint table
A target file already exists, so the proposed variant is written beside it instead

responsibilities: Record every price as a row in prices.json with a source_url and a retrieved_at date
Build the cost model from those rows only, and show the arithmetic
State a sensitivity band on the three drivers that move the total most
stop_conditions: A price cannot be traced to a public vendor page that was fetched during this run
A price row's retrieved_at is more than 90 days old
A figure would be written that is neither a fetched price nor arithmetic over fetched prices
A target file already exists, so the proposed variant is written beside it instead

responsibilities: Trace one retrieved document from retriever to context window and point at the line where it becomes labelled data
Assign every input and tool a trust tier: T0 private local, T1 scoped project, T2 external tools, T3 untrusted content
List every irreversible tool and name the human step that gates it
stop_conditions: The line where retrieved text becomes labelled data cannot be located, so the finding is recorded as ABSENT rather than guessed
An irreversible tool has no human gate, which is recorded as a finding and not repaired by editing code
A target file already exists, so the proposed variant is written beside it instead

responsibilities: Write at least ten eval cases as JSON lines, including at least one refusal case and at least one injection case
Write the grading rubric
Run the harness and record the observed output as evidence, including that the injection case fails closed
stop_conditions: Fewer than ten cases, or no refusal case, or no injection case
The harness has not been run in this session, so no observed output exists to cite
The injection case passes, meaning the system followed retrieved text as instruction
A target file already exists, so the proposed variant is written beside it instead

responsibilities: Write WORKFLOW.md with the machine-parsable stage table that the /architect router reads to pick the next stage
Write SOP.md with model routing, write scopes, stop conditions, human gates, and escalation
Write the runbook, and dry-run every command in it so the exit status is observed rather than assumed
stop_conditions: A runbook command has not been dry-run in this session
A runbook command dry-runs to a non-zero exit status and the runbook still presents it as working
A step has no named rollback or no named owner
A target file already exists, so the proposed variant is written beside it instead

responsibilities: Re-derive every evidence pointer in a fresh context, without reading any other agent's reasoning
Re-run every fenced command and compare the observed output against the recorded output
Write a dated receipt and a review, and never edit the artifacts under review
stop_conditions: A fix would be applied to a file under review rather than recorded as a failed gate
An evidence pointer resolves to a line that does not contain what was claimed, which is recorded as FAIL and not repaired
A gate would be recorded PASS on the strength of another agent's assertion rather than a re-derivation

handoff_protocol: Each agent ends with a handoff block naming the stage id, the artifacts written, the gate id, the gate status, the evidence pointers, and the next role
Evidence pointers are either path/to/file.ts:L42 or a fenced command together with its observed output
No agent writes application source code; the artifact set under docs/architecture/ is the only output
An existing file is never overwritten; the agent writes <name>.proposed.md beside it and says so in the handoff
Every generated markdown file ends with the line: Generated by AI Architect · https://www.frankx.ai/ai-architect
Implementation roles and the verification role stay independent; the Independent Verifier reads artifacts and re-derives evidence, and never edits what it reviews
architecture.json is the resumable state file; the /architect router records each stage's gate result into it, and only the Principal Architect authors its decisions, planes, and artifacts sections
